extracted.intended_audience: owners/operators of CCR units, state and federal regulators, environmental lawyers, and other stakeholders commenting on or implementing the CCR rule
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of regulatory definitions, jurisdictional tests, closure and certification requirements, and evidentiary/monitoring standards used to determine whether a CCR surface impoundment is a legacy impoundment subject to part 257 and what documentation is required to demonstrate closure or exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of "liquids" (§257.53)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Liquids means any fluid (such as water) that has no independent shape but has a definite volume and does not expand indefinitely and that is only slightly compressible.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA codifies the Merriam-Webster-derived definition to expressly encompass all types of liquids that may be present in a CCR unit, including water sluiced into an impoundment with CCR, precipitation, surface water, groundwater, and any other form of water that has migrated into the impoundment; this may be found as free water/standing ponded water above CCR or porewater intermingled with CCR. EPA declined to adopt a narrower technical or soil-physics based definition and will not generally rely on the Paint Filter Liquids Test to determine absence of free liquids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of "contains both CCR and liquids" (§257.53)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Contains both CCR and liquids means that both CCR and liquids are present in a CCR surface impoundment, except where the owner or operator demonstrates that the standard in §257.102(d)(2)(i) has been met.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition reflects the dictionary meaning of “contains” and EPA's approach to use the closure-in-place performance standard (§257.102(d)(2)(i)) as the means by which an owner/operator can demonstrate that a unit does not contain CCR and liquids for purposes of the legacy-impoundment determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legacy impoundment determination (presence on or after Oct 19, 2015)
rubrics_metrics.description: An inactive CCR surface impoundment is a legacy impoundment if it contained CCR and liquids on or after October 19, 2015.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA gives specific examples: (1) any impoundment where water flowed or continues to flow through the impoundment permeating the waste (e.g., base intersects groundwater); (2) impoundment where only surface water was decanted but waste remains saturated; and (3) any impoundment that still contains free liquids—even if closed under State law, in the process of closing on the effective date, or fully dewatered only after October 19, 2015 (i.e., it contained free liquids on Oct 19, 2015).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption for units closed by removal before Oct 19, 2015
rubrics_metrics.description: If all CCR and liquids were removed from an impoundment prior to October 19, 2015, the site is not subject to the final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Closure is complete under §257.102(c) when: all CCR has been removed from the CCR unit; any areas affected by releases from the CCR unit have been removed; and groundwater monitoring concentrations do not exceed the groundwater protection standard in §257.95(h) for Appendix IV constituents. EPA clarified it did not propose to require documentation that an impoundment did not contain liquids prior to Oct 19, 2015.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of closure by removal (documentation requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for closure certification (and exemption from further requirements), a facility must document that it meets the criteria in §257.102(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required documentation: demonstration that all CCR has been removed from the unit; any areas affected by releases have been removed; and groundwater monitoring data showing that concentrations of each Appendix IV constituent do not exceed the relevant GWPS (either the MCL or background) for two consecutive sampling events. The facility must post this documentation on its CCR website for units that completed closure by removal prior to the effective date of the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of initiating closure by removal before Oct 19, 2015 but containing CCR/liquids on or after that date
rubrics_metrics.description: A facility that initiated closure by removal prior to Oct 19, 2015 but whose impoundment still contained CCR and liquids on or after Oct 19, 2015 is considered a legacy CCR surface impoundment and regulated under the final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if the facility removed all CCR prior to the effective date of the final rule, the unit would still be a legacy impoundment if it contained CCR and liquids on or after Oct 19, 2015. Depending on when closure completes, some requirements may no longer apply, but the unit remains subject unless the closure-by-removal certification criteria are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure-in-place (§257.102(d)) standard and its evidentiary effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators may demonstrate that the standard in §257.102(d)(2)(i) has been met to show that a unit does not “contain” CCR and liquids under the definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA will not accept a simple statement of prior closure-in-place as a ground for blanket exemption from post-closure monitoring and corrective action; if a facility documents that closure-in-place meets §257.102(d), then compliance with groundwater monitoring (§§257.90–257.95) and necessary corrective action during post-closure care (plus recordkeeping/posting) are required. EPA declined commenters' requests to treat §257.102(d)-based prior closures as automatically exempt without factual support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption that residual CCR leachate remains after removal absent documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA presumes that leachate (and therefore solid waste) often remains on-site even after CCR removal, unless the facility rebuts that presumption with documentation meeting §257.102(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: older legacy units frequently lack liners, many units operate long enough to leak, and common removal verification practices (visual or microscopic inspection) are unlikely to remove or detect all affected soils or leachate. Demonstrating compliance with §257.102(c) rebuts the presumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA jurisdiction over sites with CCR removed but groundwater contamination present
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA retains jurisdiction over sites where CCR leachate remains in soil or groundwater after CCR removal because the leachate constitutes a solid waste under the statutory definition (42 U.S.C. 6903(27)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA cites precedent and statutory language: ‘discarded’ means disposed/abandoned; leaked or spilled material that remains is part of the waste disposal problem RCRA addresses. Presence of Appendix IV constituent exceedances in groundwater can demonstrate that solid waste remains on site and support jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of CCR leachate as a solid waste
rubrics_metrics.description: Leachate from a CCR surface impoundment or landfill is a solid waste under the broader statutory definition in 42 U.S.C. 6903(27).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA explains that contaminated media themselves may not be the waste, but the contamination (leachate) is a solid waste; prior case law supports considering spilled/leaked material as ‘abandoned’ or ‘discarded.’ This supports regulation of sites based on residual contamination left after physical removal of CCR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Groundwater monitoring requirement for closure documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Groundwater monitoring concentrations must not exceed the groundwater protection standard (GWPS) for Appendix IV constituents for two consecutive sampling events to demonstrate closure by removal under §257.102(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GWPS is either the MCL or background concentration as relevant. This two-sample demonstration is a condition of the closure certification that exempts the facility from further requirements under the final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of reliance on Paint Filter Liquids Test (PFLT)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA declined to adopt the PFLT-based definition (40 CFR 258.28(c)(1)) or to mandate reliance on the Paint Filter Liquids Test to determine presence/absence of liquids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA notes technical concerns raised by commenters: sampling can alter representativeness (vibration, heat, etc.) and produce false negatives; while PFLT may confirm presence of water in a sample, EPA considers it not sufficiently reliable to confirm absence of free liquids in CCR contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of porewater and measurement feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA acknowledges commenters' concerns that porewater (water held in interstices/pore spaces) can be difficult to measure and that including all porewater could make it infeasible to demonstrate absence of liquids historically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Despite measurement difficulties, EPA's adopted Merriam-Webster-derived definition of liquids explicitly encompasses porewater intermingled with CCR. EPA declined to adopt definitions that would exclude bound porewater or rely on soil-physics analogies because CCR is not a soil and hydraulic characterization differs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of a narrower ‘material in the liquid state’ test
rubrics_metrics.description: Some commenters proposed defining 'liquids' based on materials in the 'liquid state' or materials that behave as liquids and can be readily separated from the solid matrix; EPA did not adopt this narrower approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA concluded that narrowing the definition to only readily separable liquids would create misunderstandings and fail to capture water types (e.g., groundwater, porewater) relevant to determining whether an impoundment is subject to part 257; EPA instead used the broader dictionary-based definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of a de minimis quantity exemption (e.g., 75,000 tons)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA disagrees that 75,000 tons (or similar de minimis thresholds) should exempt legacy impoundments from regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA clarifies that the commenter misread the 2015 analysis; EPA did not conclude that quantities below 75,000 tons pose no risk, and therefore will not adopt a de minimis cutoff for exemption from legacy-impoundment regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation posting and scope of relief if full-site certification provided
rubrics_metrics.description: If a facility certifies that all legacy CCR surface impoundments on-site have met the requirements in §257.102(c) for closure by removal before the effective date, the facility would not be subject to any further requirements under the final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification requires posting the required documentation on the facility's CCR website. This relief applies to both legacy impoundment requirements and CCR management unit (CCRMU) requirements if the site-wide certification meets the §257.102(c) criteria.
